info.title: AeroDataBox over Airnode
info.description:
AeroDataBox is an aviation data API covering live and historical flight status, airport schedules, airport and runway reference data, and aircraft records. This Airnode wraps its read endpoints, so a consumer receives a flight's status with a signature saying this Airnode obtained it from AeroDataBox at this time, rather than trusting a copy that passed through an unnamed hop.

Whether a flight is late is a question whose answer changes by the minute, which makes it worth asking an Airnode: the attestation dates the answer as well as attributing it. Live status and estimated times only exist for airports AeroDataBox tracks, so airportFeedStatus is where to check before concluding a flight has no data.

AeroDataBox is reached through RapidAPI and the plan behind it is metered in units, with the more expensive endpoints costing many times a cheap one. The operations here are the ones that cost the least, so airport delay statistics, route statistics and flight alert webhooks are not served.

Every response carries an EIP-191 signature from the Airnode that served it, so the data can be attributed back to its source rather than trusted on reputation.

get.description: Describes the operations this Airnode serves and how to verify what it returns. Free.

200.description: An OpenAPI document describing this Airnode.

post.summary: Perform an operation and attest to the response.

oneOf.title: flightStatus
oneOf.description: The status of a flight on the nearest date it operates, past or future.

operation.description:
Live status where the airport is tracked and the flight is not far in the future, and the schedule otherwise. This is the operation to ask when the question is whether today's flight is late. Use flightStatusOnDate for a specific day.

A flight number can be operated by more than one aircraft on the same date, so the answer is a list. Parts of it may be missing: an airport AeroDataBox does not track live has scheduled times and no actual ones, and the quality markers inside the response say which is which.

searchParam.description: The flight to look up, spelled as searchBy says, such as KL1395 or BA 117 for number, PH-BXO for reg, AFL1482 for callsign, or 484161 for icao24. A flight number takes a space or not, and IATA or ICAO.

dateLocalRole.description: Whether the nearest date is read as the departure date, the arrival date or either. Both is the default and the one that finds a flight regardless of which end of it the date belongs to.

withLocation.description: Include position, altitude, speed and track for a flight currently in the air, where AeroDataBox has them.

responseProjection.description: Optional. Maps a name of your choosing to an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the upstream response, such as {"price": "/ethereum/usd"}. data is then the text of a JSON object of those names in Unicode code point order, each value as the upstream wrote it, instead of the whole body, and the projection is part of the signed request identity. No two names take the same pointer, and no pointer is inside another's value. A pointer the response does not have is a 400.

operation.description: The same answer as flightStatus for a date given rather than inferred. A date in the past returns what happened, a date in the future returns the schedule, and how far either way is bounded by AeroDataBox's coverage and the plan behind the key.

oneOf.title: airportSchedule
oneOf.description: Departures and arrivals at an airport around now.

operation.description:
The board an airport shows, over a window measured from the airport's own current time rather than from UTC. The window is offsetMinutes to offsetMinutes plus durationMinutes, so a negative offset reaches back over what has already left.

The window has an upstream maximum, and asking for a wide one at a busy airport returns a large response. Narrow it with direction and the with- flags rather than filtering afterwards, since the whole response is what gets attested.

codeType.description: Which kind of airport code the code parameter is.

code.description: The airport, spelled as codeType says, such as AMS for iata or EHAM for icao.

offsetMinutes.description: Where the window starts, in minutes relative to the airport's current local time. Negative reaches into the past.

durationMinutes.description: How long the window is, in minutes. The upstream caps it.

direction.description: Which half of the board to return. Both is the default.

withLeg.description: Include the other end of each flight, so a departure carries where it is going rather than only when it leaves.

withCodeshared.description: Include code-shared duplicates of the same physical flight.

withLocation.description: Include position, altitude, speed and track for the flights currently airborne.

responseProjection.description: Optional. oneOf.title: airportDistance
oneOf.description: Distance and estimated flight time between two airports.

operation.description: Great circle distance and how long a flight between the two typically takes. The time is a model's estimate rather than an observation, so what an attestation over it says is that AeroDataBox estimated this, at this time.

codeType.description: Which kind of airport code both codes are.

aircraftName.description: An aircraft type as free text. Taken into account where it can be, which sharpens the flight time.

flightTimeModel.description: Which model estimates the flight time. Standard is distance and typical speed; ML01 leans on the recent history of the route and falls back to Standard when it has too little to work with.

oneOf.description: Which data feeds AeroDataBox has for an airport.

operation.description: Whether an airport has schedules only, live status updates, or ADS-B derived updates. This is the difference between a flight having no data and a flight not being tracked, and it is the cheapest call here, so it is the one to make before reading anything into a thin answer from a flight operation.

200.description: The upstream response and the attestation over it.

400.description: The operation exists but the parameters or the projection are missing, unknown or malformed, a path parameter is empty, . or .. or has such a part between slashes, or the projection names too many fields, an empty or repeated pointer, or a path the response does not have. Also a PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header that does not decode to a payment payload.

402.description: The operation is paid and no valid payment was supplied. The PAYMENT-REQUIRED header carries the x402 payment requirements to retry against.

502.description: The upstream API could not be reached or refused the request.

airnode.description: The address whose signature attests to this response.

requestHash.description: Identifies the request this response answers.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds at which the response was signed.

data.description: The upstream response body exactly as received, less a leading byte order mark. With a projection, the text of a JSON object keyed by the names it asked for in Unicode code point order, each value as the upstream wrote it.

attestation.digest: keccak256(abi.encodePacked(bytes32 requestHash, uint256 timestamp, bytes dataBytes))
attestation.requestHash: keccak256(utf8(JSON.stringify([operation, parameterEntriesSortedByName]))), where an object value is itself entries sorted by name, at any depth, and an array keeps its order. Names are compared by Unicode code point. A request that carries a projection appends its entries, sorted the same way, as a third element
attestation.verify: Recover the signer of the signature over the digest and check it equals the address above.

parameters.x-airnode-sign: false skips the signature: no attestation headers, and the body streamed through with no size cap.
parameters.x-airnode-project: alias:pointer, once per field to keep and at most 20 times, each pointer an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the upstream response that starts with /, is not repeated and is not inside another's value. The body becomes an object of those aliases in Unicode code point order, the signature covers it, and a pointer the response does not have is a 400.

passthrough.flow: Send the request the provider documents, method, path, query and body as they are, to url followed by the route's path. The body comes back as the upstream sent it, with the upstream's status, and on success the attestation is in the X-Airnode-Address, X-Airnode-Request-Hash, X-Airnode-Timestamp and X-Airnode-Signature headers, with the operation served in X-Airnode-Operation. Every query parameter starting with x-airnode- is this Airnode's own, listed under parameters, and never reaches the upstream.
passthrough.requestHash: keccak256(utf8(JSON.stringify(["passthrough", method, path, queryEntries, headerEntries, body]))), where method is upper case, path is what was sent after url as a URL parser resolves it, the query entries are what was sent with the Airnode's own parameters removed, in the order sent, headerEntries are the headers that the routes declare as parameters and the request sent, each name in lower case and sorted by Unicode code point, with the values of a header sent more than once joined with ", " in the order sent and the result trimmed of spaces and tabs, and body is the request body as sent, or an empty string. A request that carries a projection appends its entries, sorted by name in Unicode code point order, as a seventh element
passthrough.dataBytes: UTF-8 of the response body exactly as received, less a leading byte order mark, or of the projected object

payment.flow: An unpaid call to a priced operation returns 402 with the x402 payment requirements, base64-encoded, in the PAYMENT-REQUIRED header. Sign an EIP-3009 authorization matching one entry and retry the call with the payment payload, base64-encoded, in the PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header. The settlement receipt comes back in the PAYMENT-RESPONSE header.
